ENFORCEMENT RULE OF THE ACT ON THE PREVENTION OF INSOLVENCY AND STRUCTURAL IMPROVEMENT OF FISHERIES COOPERATIVES

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Rule is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on the Prevention of Insolvency and Structural Improvement of Fisheries Cooperatives.

Article 2 (Methods of Evaluating Management Status)
(1) Management status under the latter sentence of subparagraph 3 (a) of Article 2 of the Act on the Prevention of Insolvency and Structural Improvement of Fisheries Cooperatives (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") shall be evaluated as follows:
1. Evaluation by sector: Evaluation of a cooperative's management status in terms of capital adequacy, asset soundness, profitability, and liquidity, based on the year-end financial results for the preceding year;
2. Comprehensive evaluation: Evaluation by integrating the sector evaluations under subparagraph 1.
(2) The grades for the evaluation by sector under paragraph (1) 1 (hereinafter referred to as "sector evaluation") and the comprehensive evaluation under subparagraph 2 of that paragraph (hereinafter referred to as "comprehensive evaluation") shall each be classified into five grades: Grade 1 (excellent), Grade 2 (good), Grade 3 (fair), Grade 4 (vulnerable), and Grade 5 (at risk).
(3) Sector evaluations shall be conducted using quantified indicators to ensure objectivity and transparency.
(4) Details concerning methods of evaluating management status, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (3), shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 3 (Standards for Evaluating and Calculating Liabilities and Assets)
(1) Liabilities and assets under the latter sentence of Article 2, subparagraph 3 (a) of the Act shall be evaluated and calculated based on the actual value of the property.
(2) Details concerning the types of liabilities and assets under paragraph (1) and the standards for evaluating and calculating them shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 4 (Financial Status Standards for Cooperatives at Risk of Insolvency)
In Article 2, subparagraph 4 of the Act, "a cooperative that is highly likely to become an insolvent cooperative because its financial status falls below the standards prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries" means a cooperative falling under any of the following:
1. A cooperative whose net capital to total assets ratio is less than 2 percent;
2. A cooperative whose comprehensive evaluation grade is Grade 4 or worse, or whose comprehensive evaluation grade is Grade 3 or better but whose sector evaluation grade for capital adequacy or asset soundness is Grade 4 or worse;
3. A cooperative that is clearly expected to fall under subparagraph 1 or 2 as a result of a financial incident or the occurrence of nonperforming loans.

Article 5 (Methods of Evaluating Management Risk)
(1) The management risk evaluation under Article 3-2 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "management risk evaluation") shall be conducted as of the last day of each month by the following methods:
1. Predicting the level of management risk by identifying changes and other developments in specific businesses in which insolvency is likely to occur;
2. Predicting the level of management risk in each sector using indicators such as capital adequacy, asset soundness, and profitability, and classifying each sector into six grades, from Grade 1 through Grade 6.
(2) Management risk grades under Article 3-2 (2) of the Act shall be determined by integrating the evaluation results under paragraph (1) and classifying management risk into six grades, from Grade 1 through Grade 6, in ascending order of risk.
(3) Notifications and reports under Article 3-2 (3) of the Act shall be made by electronic document within seven days after the date on which the management risk evaluation is completed. However, where the Federation registers the results of the management risk evaluation in the insolvency prevention system under Article 3 (2) of the Act, it may dispense with separate notification to the cooperative.

Article 6 (Criteria for Designating Cooperatives Subject to Management Control)
In Article 3-3 (1) 1 of the Act, "where the criteria prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries are met" means any of the following:
1. Grade 4 or worse for nine consecutive months;
2. Grade 5 or worse for six consecutive months;
3. Grade 6 for three consecutive months.

Article 7 (Submission of Management Improvement Plans)
Where a cooperative designated as subject to management control under Article 3-3 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "cooperative subject to management control") is requested to submit a management improvement plan under Article 3-4 (1) of the Act, it shall submit the plan to the head of the management agency within 30 days after the date of receipt of the request.

Article 8 (Cooperatives Subject to Management Control That Are Subject to Corrective Requirements)
In the former sentence of Article 3-4 (2) of the Act, excluding its subparagraphs, "a cooperative meeting the criteria prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries" means a cooperative falling under any of the following:
1. A cooperative whose management risk grade under Article 3-2 (2) of the Act is Grade 6 and whose financial status is at risk of further deterioration, such as where its evaluation score has declined for six or more consecutive months;
2. A cooperative whose net capital to total assets ratio is at risk of falling below 2 percent;
3. A cooperative whose sector evaluation grade for asset soundness under Article 5 (1) 2 is at risk of falling to Grade 4 or worse because of an increase in the delinquency rate of its credit business.

Article 9 (Procedures for Corrective Requirements)
(1) An action plan under the latter sentence of Article 3-4 (2) of the Act, excluding its subparagraphs, shall be submitted to the head of the management agency within 30 days after the date on which the corrective requirement is received.
(2) Where the head of the management agency determines that an action plan submitted under paragraph (1) does not specifically reflect the corrective requirement or cannot be implemented, the head may request that the plan be revised or supplemented.
(3) The head of the management agency shall notify the cooperative concerned of the termination of the corrective requirement under Article 3-4 (4) of the Act within seven days after the date of the decision to terminate it.

Article 10 (Keeping, Managing, and Inspecting Materials Concerning Contract Transfers)
The standards and procedures necessary for keeping, managing, and inspecting materials concerning contract transfers under the latter sentence of Article 11 (6) of the Act are prescribed in the attached Table.

Article 11 (Appointment of Administrators)
The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may appoint an executive officer or employee of the Federation as an administrator upon the recommendation of the head of the management agency under the main sentence of Article 12 (2) of the Act.

ADDENDA <Ordinance No. 424, August 19, 2020>

This Rule shall enter into force on August 19, 2020.

ENFORCEMENT RULE OF THE ACT ON THE PREVENTION OF INSOLVENCY AND STRUCTURAL IMPROVEMENT OF FISHERIES COOPERATIVES [ATTACHED TABLE]

Standards and Procedures Necessary for Keeping, Managing, and Inspecting Materials Concerning Contract Transfers (Related to Article 10)

1. Keeping and managing materials: The insolvent cooperative concerned and the acquiring cooperative for which a decision on a contract transfer has been made shall each keep and manage materials concerning the contract transfer at their respective principal offices.

2. Inspection of materials
(a) Persons entitled to request inspection of materials concerning a contract transfer shall be limited to interested parties themselves, such as creditors involved in the contract transfer, and their agents. A cooperative receiving a request for inspection shall verify whether the requester is the interested party or a duly authorized agent.
(b) The following materials shall be excluded from inspection requests:
1) Materials classified as secret or prescribed as nonpublic under an Act;
2) Materials relating to matters in the decision-making process or under internal review, for which there are substantial grounds to believe that permitting inspection would significantly hinder the fair performance of duties;
3) Other materials for which permitting inspection is considered likely to significantly harm the legitimate interests of a related corporation, organization, or individual.
(c) A request to inspect materials shall be made by submitting a written document stating the contents of the materials and the purpose of their use to the principal office of the cooperative keeping and managing them. In such cases, the cooperative shall decide whether to permit inspection and notify the requester without delay; notification of a refusal to permit inspection shall be in writing and state the reasons for refusal.
(d) A requester notified of a refusal to permit inspection may file a written objection with the management agency within 30 days after the date of receiving that notification.
(e) Inspection of materials shall be provided by such methods as allowing inspection at a designated time and place or furnishing copies.
(f) A cooperative shall record and manage the status of its handling of requests to inspect materials.
